name: Web Directory Free – AI powered
author: Shamalli

sections.description:
Web Directory Free is a WordPress directory plugin that turns your site into a searchable business directory. Sort listings into categories and locations, build your own listing form, drop the directory onto any page with a shortcode, and let visitors search and browse – as a list, as cards, or on an interactive map.

In the free edition you add and edit listings from the WordPress admin, and visitors browse, search and view them on the front end.

AI that writes the listing, and search by sentence

Add a key for a free AI service and a Write button appears beside the listing description: it reads the entry name, its categories and its location, and drafts the text. Nothing is sent anywhere until you enter that key, and the fields a person has to state as fact – prices, phone numbers, dates, opening hours – are never generated, because a plausible invented price is worse than an empty one.

The free edition ships with Groq, which has a free tier that needs no payment card. The separate AI Assistant Add-on widens it: OpenAI, DeepSeek, Mistral, OpenRouter and Google Gemini as further services, a Write button on every text field on the form instead of the description alone, and one control that fills every empty field in a single request so the texts agree with each other.

The add-on also brings assisted search. A visitor writes what they are after as a sentence, “a cheap place open on Sunday that takes cards”, and it is read into the search form’s own filters rather than into the keyword box: the category, the location and the distance, the sliders and the dropdowns your form carries. Only values the form actually offers are set, every one of them is shown above the results as a chip the visitor can drop, and a filter they set or cleared themselves is left exactly as they left it. A one-word search is answered the way it always was, without asking the model at all. The add-on is a plugin of its own and is managed from the same AI settings tab.

Live demo: directory.salephpscripts.com

What you can build

A local business directory, a member or staff directory, a property or vehicle catalogue, a venue or event guide, a service-provider index, a classifieds board. Anything that is a list of places or things with fields, categories and a map.

Organise your listings

  • Categories and locations are hierarchical, so Country, Region, City nests the way you expect, and each level gets its own page.
  • Each category can carry its own marker icon and colour, so the map reads at a glance.
  • Every category and location page is a real URL with its own listings, search and map.

Build the listing form yourself

The form builder is drag and drop: arrange fields in rows and columns, and add your own on top of the built-in ones. Field types included:

  • Title, Content, Excerpt
  • Categories
  • Address and Map
  • Images & Videos – photos plus YouTube or Vimeo links, shown in one gallery with a lightbox
  • Contact info, Phone, Email, Website URL
  • Text/string, Number, Price
  • List – as a dropdown, radio buttons or checkboxes
  • Date-Time
  • Opening hours
  • File upload

Every field can be placed independently on the listing card, the listing page, the search form and the map popup, so a field can be searchable without cluttering the card.

Put the directory anywhere

Each directory has a page builder: choose which elements appear on the home, category, location and listing pages, and in what order – search form, map, categories block, listings grid, slider, breadcrumbs, page title, buttons.

If you would rather place things by hand, every element is also a shortcode: [webdirectory], [webdirectory-search], [webdirectory-map], [webdirectory-listings], [webdirectory-categories], [webdirectory-locations], [webdirectory-slider], [webdirectory-breadcrumbs], [webdirectory-listing-page] and more. They work in the block editor, in Elementor and in WPBakery.

Maps

  • Three engines: Google Maps, Mapbox and MapLibre with MapTiler tiles. Pick per site.
  • Marker clustering, so thousands of listings stay usable.
  • Per-category and per-listing marker icons.
  • Rich popups built from the fields you chose, with the listing photo.
  • A map sidebar that lists what is currently in view, and follows as the visitor pans.
  • Radius search from an address, in miles or kilometres.
  • Several layouts, including a full-width hero map and a sticky map beside the listings.

Search that finds things

The search form is built the same way as the listing form: drag in the elements you want.

  • Keyword, categories, locations, address plus radius, rating.
  • Any custom field you added becomes a filter – a price range, a number range, a date, a dropdown.
  • A “More filters” separator to keep the visible form short.
  • Sorting by newest, oldest, title, rating, random, or any numeric or date field you defined.
  • Grid and list views, with the visitor’s choice remembered.
  • With the AI Assistant Add-on, a whole sentence instead of a form: the filters above set themselves from it, and the visitor can drop any of them.

Ratings

Built in, no add-on: visitors rate a listing, the average shows on the card, the listing page and the map popup, and rating becomes a search filter and a sort option. Ratings can be switched off entirely.

Bulk work

  • CSV import and export for listings, including categories, locations, custom fields, images and video links. Import creates or updates; export round-trips.
  • Demo content: 5 ready-made directories with their maps and pages, and a listing form template, imported in one click.
  • A thumbnail regeneration tool for when you change image sizes.

Housekeeping

  • Colour palette controls so the directory matches your theme, with several presets.
  • Email notifications with editable subjects, each one switchable.
  • Google reCAPTCHA (v2 or v3) on the listing contact form.
  • A diagnostics page that checks the directory is wired up correctly and tells you what to fix if it is not.
  • An install wizard that creates the pages and the first directory for you.
  • Translation ready: ships a POT file for any standard gettext or PO editor.
  • Built for large directories: a dedicated search index and sort index keep tens of thousands of listings responsive, and both rebuild in the background.

This plugin uses external services (map providers and, if you enable it, Google reCAPTCHA). See the External Services section below.

What is not in the free edition

Front-end submission. In the free edition listings are created and edited in the WordPress admin; visitors browse and search. The paid version adds front-end submission with membership plans, listing expiry and renewals, and WooCommerce checkout for paid, featured and upgraded listings.

Get the full version: Web 2.0 Directory on CodeCanyon

External Services

Web Directory Free uses the following third-party services. Nothing is sent until you use the matching feature:

  • Map providers (Google Maps, Mapbox, MapTiler / MapLibre) – when a map loads or an address is geocoded, the request (coordinates, the address being searched, and your API key/token) is sent to the provider you chose. See that provider’s terms and privacy policy.
  • Google reCAPTCHA – when you turn it on for the contact form, the visitor’s interaction is checked with Google. See Google’s terms and privacy policy.
  • Groq (AI writing) – only when you have entered a Groq API key and pressed a Write button. What is sent is the text the draft is built from: the entry name, its categories, its location and the fields already filled in. Nothing is sent without a key, and no key ships with the plugin. See Groq’s terms (https://groq.com/terms-of-use/) and privacy policy (https://groq.com/privacy-policy/).

The free edition does not contact the author’s servers: it gets updates through WordPress.org and does no license or “phone-home” checks.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP via Plugins -> Add New -> Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate Web Directory Free from the Plugins menu.
  3. Open the settings page, pick your map engine and enter its API key/token (Google Maps API key, Mapbox token, or MapTiler key).
  4. Create your categories and locations, build the listing form, add listings, and place the directory on any page with the shortcode.
sections.faq:
Who can add listings in the free edition?

Listings are created and edited from the WordPress admin. Front-end submission (with optional moderation, expiration and renewal) is part of the full version.

Do I need API keys?

For maps, yes – each map provider needs its own key/token, entered on the settings page. Keys are stored on your site and are never sent to us.

Which map providers are supported?

Google Maps, Mapbox, and MapLibre with MapTiler tiles. You pick one on the settings page.

Is it translation ready?

Yes. A languages/w2dc.pot template is included; translate it with any standard gettext/PO editor.

How do paid listings and membership plans work?

Paid submission, membership plans and WooCommerce checkout come with the full version of Web 2.0 Directory, not the free edition.

2.3.3 – 2026-10-01

  • New: a Sort options table for the Listings element: choose which orders the visitor’s Sort control offers, in what order and direction, under what name, whether sticky listings go first, and which one the grid opens with.
  • New: switching a directory’s Listing template rebuilds the settings that list its fields (card fields, sort options, Listing body, default filter, search form). Switching back brings the old template’s settings back.
  • New: a Default image for listings that have none, shown on their card, in the map popup and in the map sidebar. A neutral built-in image by default; choose your own or switch it off. Sites moved over from the old Web 2.0 Directory keep their default logo.
  • Improvement: sorting by title no longer puts sticky listings first by default. Turn it on for Title in Sort options if you want it.
  • Improvement: more space between the fields of the listing form.
  • Improvement: the demo maps import with “Save and follow map center” off, so moving one no longer rewrites the page address.
  • Improvement: a field added to the listing form after the Listing body’s field list was saved now shows on the listing page too.
  • Improvement: the Rating row of the Listing body starts switched off, so the listing page no longer shows the rating twice.
  • Improvement: the map’s cookie-consent notice can be translated, names the consent plugin holding the map back (Borlabs Cookie, Complianz, Cookiebot or Avada Privacy) and, with Borlabs Cookie or Cookiebot, has an Open cookie settings button.
  • Improvement: buttons and links in the Edit Directory boxes use the primary colour set in Customization instead of the WordPress admin blue.
  • Improvement: a word limit for every text field on the listing cards: 10 words for the title and 20 for the others by default (0 shows the whole text).
  • Improvement: categories, tags and list fields on the cards show 5 items by default (0 shows all) and end with …; hover it to see how many more there are.
  • Improvement: in the field lists of Edit Directory and Edit Map the options line up in one column, and the Popups list’s “fill” switch matches the on/off one.
  • Improvement: category markers, listing markers and image markers each have their own size in Edit Map (30-70 px, 40 by default). Existing maps keep their old size.
  • Improvement: map popups and the map sidebar cut long content like the cards do: 20 words for text fields (10 for the title) and 5 items for categories, tags and lists, set per row in Edit Map (0 shows everything).
  • Improvement: the translation template (.pot) now lists every string of the plugin, the new screens included, so the whole interface can be translated.
  • Fix: a directory on any form template but the first showed the first template’s fields in the builder, on its cards and Sort control, and on its listing pages.
  • Fix: a Mapbox or MapLibre map held back by a cookie-consent plugin says it is waiting for consent instead of “API key is not configured”, and appears as soon as the visitor accepts.
  • Fix: on a site that finished migrating, the migration screen no longer offers the Plans step again (running it overwrote the plans set up since).
  • Fix: a new listing form starts with the standard fields (title, description, excerpt, categories, tags, address, map, images). On sites moved over from the old Web 2.0 Directory it started with every old field.
  • Fix: on Google Maps, markers and clusters no longer disappear while the map pans.
  • Fix: the open/close tab of the map sidebar keeps its shape on themes that round every button.
  • Fix: the number fields in the Edit Map and Edit Directory field lists show two-digit values in full.
  • Fix: directory pages with an element stretched over several rows, like the demo listing pages, stack into one column on tablets and phones.
  • Fix: the Price field on the listing page lines up with the other fields on phones and on wide screens.
  • Fix: on phones the map’s “Number of locations” counter no longer hides under the sidebar tab or the attribution button.
  • Fix: on phones the “AI-assisted search” label of a search form on the map is no longer cut off.

2.3.2 – 2026-09-28

  • New: three ways to choose categories on the listing form, set per form: a checkbox list, dropdowns level by level, or type-to-search where you can also add a category that does not exist yet, the way tags work. Existing forms keep what they had.
  • New: the form builder places fields on the same grid as the directory builder. Every field and group carries its own width buttons – full, 2/3, 1/2, 1/3 – so a field can be made wide where it sits instead of only as the first slot of a two-thirds row, and arrow buttons stretch a field down over the empty space below it, which keeps the column beside it from sliding under. Templates saved before this open and save unchanged.
  • New: the plan option “Enable map” is a real switch. Off, a listing of that plan gets no map on its page and no map field on the listing form; the address still places it. Existing plans keep their map: the option is stamped on as it was.
  • Improvement: with no Map field on the listing form, no map is drawn anywhere – there is nothing behind it. A listing with no plan follows the form.
  • Improvement: the price on a listing page can be styled the way it already could on cards – its own size, a badge, a rule above and below, an accent bar, a smaller currency sign. Set per element, in the Listing body element’s field list.
  • Improvement: a field stretched down in the builder fills that space on the form too – a tall category list, map or text box instead of a gap under a short field.
  • Improvement: the AI buttons all look alike and say why they are not ready yet: the “fill in the title and choose a category” note is now in one place, on the Write-all bar, instead of under every field.
  • Improvement: field groups on the listing form open and close smoothly instead of blinking out.
  • Improvement: the listing form is easier to read: field names are bold, fields side by side start at the same height, and the video link box is as tall as every other input.
  • Improvement: renewing a listing adds the plan’s period to the time it still has, instead of starting from the day of renewal. Renewing early no longer costs the remaining days; a listing renewed after it expired still gets a full period from that day.
  • Improvement: the price caption on a plan card follows the plan’s own active period when it is left empty, so a card cannot promise “per year” on a plan whose listings live a month. Your own wording still wins if you set it.
  • Improvement: every number on a plan is a limit now, and the limit a listing gets. 0 means none – no images, no videos, no address, no categories, no tags – as it did in the earlier version and as the plan card already said, instead of quietly handing the listing form’s own limit back; a listing shows at most as many images and videos as its plan allows, the form’s own limits apply only to a listing with no plan, and plans that never carried a number keep exactly what they had.
  • Improvement: the listing form in wp-admin is wider, up to 1100px instead of 768px, so the fields use the box rather than a narrow column down the middle of it. Most noticeable on a screen set to one column, where the box is the full width of the page.
  • Improvement: ticking Closed or 24h in Opening hours no longer loses the day’s times while the form is open. Unticking puts them back, so a day switched on and off again does not have to be entered twice.
  • Improvement: reloading a listing form, or saving one in wp-admin, no longer throws the page back to the top. The form remembers how tall it was and how far down the page stood, and puts both back as the fields arrive, instead of leaving the view to be restored against a page that is still empty.
  • Fix: “N listings included” is shown only on plans that can actually grant the package, which needs the full version’s payments. In the free version the line is no longer printed; the setting itself is kept.
  • Fix: a listing shows only the fields its plan includes – on its page, in map popups, the sidebar, cards and marker labels. A listing moved to a smaller plan, by hand or when a paid period ran out, went on showing the fields it no longer paid for; they come back if it returns to the plan.
  • Fix: a listing can no longer be saved with a field its plan does not include. The form already hid such fields, but the server accepted them.
  • Fix: the plan’s Logo enabled switch, now next to Images number, works. Turned off, that plan’s listings show no logo on cards, in map popups, the map sidebar or on image markers, and the listing form stops offering a logo choice; plans migrated from the earlier version get back the setting their level had.
  • Fix: on Settings, Plans the “show as feature” checkboxes sit on the field’s label line again instead of on top of the input below.
  • Fix: the plan option “Who can view listings” works. A visitor the plan shuts out opens the listing page and sees its title with a note instead of the content; the listing itself stays in the directory, the search and the map. Before, the setting was saved but never applied.
  • Fix: a plan’s “Certain locations” is enforced when a listing is saved, not only in the form. A location outside the plan’s list is dropped from the address instead of being stored; the address itself is kept.
  • Fix: the plan groups in the plans constructor are shaded again, so each group reads as a block.
  • Fix: a plan’s limits on categories and tags now hold on every save, not only in the listing form: quick edit, bulk edit, a CSV import and a programmatic save are clamped too, and the “Certain categories” subset with them.
  • Fix: a plan with “Logo enabled” off no longer shows the logo in the map’s info window or as the page’s share image; every other surface already honoured it.
  • Fix: on WPML and Polylang sites a translated listing follows its plan’s limits. The plan is stored on the main version, so a translation read as having no plan at all.
  • Fix: a plan with “Listings have own pages” off really leaves its listings without one: the listing URL answers 404 instead of opening the page, and the slider stops linking to it. Before, only the title on a card was unlinked while the page stayed open to anyone with the link.
  • Fix: the plans box on Edit Directory fits a narrow column. Each plan keeps its whole name on the first line, next to Expand, and its summary moves to a line of its own, instead of the name shrinking to three letters and the summary standing in a column. On Settings, Plans the plan changes table scrolls inside the page instead of pushing the plans past its right edge.
  • Fix: the “Use gradient on buttons” option works again: the main buttons fade from the button primary color to the button secondary color, reversed on hover, and keep their icons.
  • Fix: importing the demo listing form no longer empties your listing form, which left listing cards showing only the image and imported listings without their custom fields. A form already emptied this way gets the default fields back.
  • Fix: demo directories keep their card fields and other element settings after import.
  • Fix: “Geocode addresses” in the CSV import now puts listings on the map from their address, with Google, Mapbox or MapTiler. Addresses it cannot place are listed in the import results.

2.3.1 – 2026-09-22

  • New: the price can stand out in map popups, the sidebar and cards: badge, divider, accent colour, smaller currency sign and font size. On cards, a price placed last sits on the bottom edge, so prices line up.
  • New: “Hide from anonymous users” for field groups. Logged-out visitors see the group title and a login prompt instead. Migrated groups keep this setting.
  • New: WPML and Polylang support. Maps, listings, search and counts show the page’s language. Each listing keeps one set of markers and one search-index entry for all its languages. Listing fields are copied to translations.
  • New: settings per language on WPML and Polylang sites. Emails, AI prompts, the address format, the map language and a few more can differ per language. Emails go out in the listing’s language.

  • Fix: sorting by date is correct on sites not in UTC.
  • Fix: the CSV import reads the image captions column.
  • Fix: map popups no longer indent fields without an icon.
  • Fix: a field with its icon turned off no longer leaves a gap.
  • Fix: the “Get directions” button looks right again.
  • Fix: fields line up with icons in the map sidebar and on cards.
  • Fix: other plugins’ links on a listing page keep their own colours.

  • Fix: the two handles of a price or number slider can no longer meet.
  • Fix: the REST SQL profile (?w2dc_sql_debug=1) works after redirects and can be turned on from an admin page.

  • Fix: no grey gap under the wizard bar on the Form Builder step.

One button on that tab, with no trip to the Plugins screen; the zip is still there to download if your server will not let WordPress write to its own plugins folder.   • Improvement: a price is shown in bold and in the primary colour, so the number a visitor is looking for stands out from the rest of the card.

Earlier versions

Each directory has a page builder: choose which elements appear on the home, category, location and listing pages, and in what order – search form, map, categories block, listings grid, slider, breadcrumbs, page title, buttons.

If you would rather place things by hand, every element is also a shortcode: [webdirectory], [webdirectory-search], [webdirectory-map], [webdirectory-listings], [webdirectory-categories], [webdirectory-locations], [webdirectory-slider], [webdirectory-breadcrumbs], [webdirectory-listing-page] and more. They work in the block editor, in Elementor and in WPBakery.

Maps

  • Three engines: Google Maps, Mapbox and MapLibre with MapTiler tiles. Pick per site.
  • Marker clustering, so thousands of listings stay usable.
  • Per-category and per-listing marker icons.
  • Rich popups built from the fields you chose, with the listing photo.
  • A map sidebar that lists what is currently in view, and follows as the visitor pans.
  • Radius search from an address, in miles or kilometres.
  • Several layouts, including a full-width hero map and a sticky map beside the listings.

Search that finds things

The search form is built the same way as the listing form: drag in the elements you want.

  • Keyword, categories, locations, address plus radius, rating.
  • Any custom field you added becomes a filter – a price range, a number range, a date, a dropdown.
  • A “More filters” separator to keep the visible form short.
  • Sorting by newest, oldest, title, rating, random, or any numeric or date field you defined.
  • Grid and list views, with the visitor’s choice remembered.
  • With the AI Assistant Add-on, a whole sentence instead of a form: the filters above set themselves from it, and the visitor can drop any of them.

Ratings

Built in, no add-on: visitors rate a listing, the average shows on the card, the listing page and the map popup, and rating becomes a search filter and a sort option. Ratings can be switched off entirely.

Bulk work

  • CSV import and export for listings, including categories, locations, custom fields, images and video links. Import creates or updates; export round-trips.
  • Demo content: 5 ready-made directories with their maps and pages, and a listing form template, imported in one click.
  • A thumbnail regeneration tool for when you change image sizes.

Housekeeping

  • Colour palette controls so the directory matches your theme, with several presets.
  • Email notifications with editable subjects, each one switchable.
  • Google reCAPTCHA (v2 or v3) on the listing contact form.
  • A diagnostics page that checks the directory is wired up correctly and tells you what to fix if it is not.
  • An install wizard that creates the pages and the first directory for you.
  • Translation ready: ships a POT file for any standard gettext or PO editor.
  • Built for large directories: a dedicated search index and sort index keep tens of thousands of listings responsive, and both rebuild in the background.

This plugin uses external services (map providers and, if you enable it, Google reCAPTCHA). See the External Services section below.

What is not in the free edition

Front-end submission. In the free edition listings are created and edited in the WordPress admin; visitors browse and search. The paid version adds front-end submission with membership plans, listing expiry and renewals, and WooCommerce checkout for paid, featured and upgraded listings.

Get the full version: Web 2.0 Directory on CodeCanyon

External Services

Web Directory Free uses the following third-party services. Nothing is sent until you use the matching feature:

  • Map providers (Google Maps, Mapbox, MapTiler / MapLibre) – when a map loads or an address is geocoded, the request (coordinates, the address being searched, and your API key/token) is sent to the provider you chose. See that provider’s terms and privacy policy.
  • Google reCAPTCHA – when you turn it on for the contact form, the visitor’s interaction is checked with Google. See Google’s terms and privacy policy.
  • Groq (AI writing) – only when you have entered a Groq API key and pressed a Write button. What is sent is the text the draft is built from: the entry name, its categories, its location and the fields already filled in. Nothing is sent without a key, and no key ships with the plugin. See Groq’s terms (https://groq.com/terms-of-use/) and privacy policy (https://groq.com/privacy-policy/).

The free edition does not contact the author’s servers: it gets updates through WordPress.org and does no license or “phone-home” checks.
